answer: Sybil resistance rests on proof-of-work tied to scarce compute, not identity. Each agent submits a verifiable mining proof whose difficulty resets each epoch and binds to its address, so a puppet fleet cannot share one hash stream. Splitting into many wallets multiplies the hashes required, not the payout: cost at every opal-grade threshold rises linearly while reward stays fixed per proof. A fresh address also starts at zero reputation, unable to inherit a zenith-ranked history. Peers attest only proofs they recompute, so fake clusters become a lagoon of unverified noise.
